## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Koraṇḍiyajātaka* (Ja 356), also titled *The Student Koraṇḍiya* and attested in edition variants as the *Kārandiyajātaka*, is a story in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. In its framing narrative set at Jetavana, the Buddha relates the story concerning the "Captain of the Faith," the elder Sāriputta [SuttaCentral]. The elder was accustomed to preaching the moral law to unvirtuous people such as hunters and fishermen, who accepted the law out of respect for him but were unable to observe it and returned to their occupations [SuttaCentral]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) of the Jātaka, the Buddha explains that Sāriputta was the teacher (brāhmaṇa) of that past lifetime, while the Bodhisatta was the pupil Koraṇḍiya (Kāraṇḍiyamāṇava) [Fausböll 1883].

SuttaCentral notes four modern translations in four languages and records no external parallels [SuttaCentral]. In text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus identifies six matching passages (amounting to 571 characters) between the canonical verses and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (longest match at §3.3–4.4 to §1460–1461), with no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [DharmaNexus].
